## Overview

Integrated supply chain analytics framework built on **3 years of daily demand data (2022–2024)** for a single SKU. Links demand uncertainty through to inventory decisions, labor allocation, and cost risk — each step's output feeds the next.

---

## Project Structure

```
├── supply_chain_data.xlsx     # Raw data (3 sheets) + Parameters & Assumptions
├── Data_Analysis.ipynb        # EDA, normality testing, transformations, seasonality
├── Forecast_Models.ipynb      # 6 models, train/test split, rolling cross-validation
├── forecast.ipynb             # Final HW-Additive fit + Monte Carlo parameters
└── outputs/
    └── demand_yeo_johnson.csv
```

    → Train/Test Evaluation → HW-Additive Selected → Forecast → Monte Carlo Params

## Distribution Analysis  ·  `Data_Analysis.ipynb`

Raw demand is **not normally distributed** (Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.0065). Four transformations were tested; **Yeo-Johnson** was selected (p = 0.0847 — fails to reject normality).

![Distribution](data:image/png;base64,)

| Transformation | Shapiro p | Selected |
|---|---|---|
| Raw | 0.0065 | ❌ |
| Square Root | 0.0182 | ❌ |
| Log | 0.0341 | ❌ |
| **Yeo-Johnson** | **0.0847** | **✅** |

> Forecasting models use the **original** demand values. Yeo-Johnson validates that residuals are approximately normal — justifying `Normal(μ, σ)` in Monte Carlo simulation.

## Forecasting Models  ·  `Forecast_Models.ipynb`

Six models fitted on monthly aggregated data (36 months). **Last 6 months held out as test set** — metrics computed on data the model never saw during training.

![Model Comparison](data:image/png;base64,)

| Model | Train MAPE | Test MAPE | CV MAPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Moving Average (w=3) | 8.5% | 5.1% | 8.2% |
| **Holt-Winters Additive** ✓ | **0.9%** | **1.7%** | **2.5%** |
| Holt-Winters Multiplicative | 0.9% | 1.9% | 2.1% |
| Polynomial Regression | 1.0% | 1.8% | 1.9% |
| Cosine Regression (K=1) | 3.7% | 4.3% | 5.0% |
| Fourier Regression (K=3) | 2.7% | 1.8% | 3.0% |

**HW-Additive selected** — lowest test MAPE (1.7%), minimal train/test gap, purpose-built for trend + seasonal data.

---

## Forecast & Monte Carlo Parameters  ·  `forecast.ipynb`

Model refitted on all 36 months. Residual std dev used as σ for simulation.

![Forecast](data:image/png;base64,)

| | |
|---|---|
| Forecast (Jan 2025) | **241.02 units/day** |
| Std Dev (σ) | **6.77 units/day** |
| 95% Prediction Interval | [227.75, 254.29] |
| Monte Carlo input | `np.random.normal(241.02, 6.77, size=(10_000, 31))` |

## Inventory Optimization  ·  `supply_chain_data.xlsx`

Implemented as **live Excel formulas** in the Parameters & Assumptions sheet.

| | Formula | Result |
|---|---|---|
| EOQ | `=SQRT(2×D×S/H)` | ~2,121 units |
| Safety Stock | `=Z × σ_daily × √L` | ~108 units (95% SL) |
| Reorder Point | `=d̄ × L + SS` | ~1,756 units |
| Annual Inventory Cost | Ordering + Holding | ~$10,606 |

Parameters: D = 75,000 units/yr · S = $150/order · H = $5/unit/yr · L = 9 days · Z = 1.645

---

## Workforce Allocation  ·  `supply_chain_data.xlsx` (Excel Solver)

Linear programming via Excel Solver. Minimizes daily labor cost subject to:
- Productivity: 12 units/labor-hour
- Regular: $18/hr (max 8 hrs/worker) · Overtime: $27/hr (max 3 hrs/worker)
- Workers: min 3, max 20 per shift
- Demand constraint: output ≥ forecasted daily demand
